claim: Piezo1 is a mechanically activated ion channel involved in sensing forces in various cell types and tissues.
source: Piezo1 is a mechanically activated ion channel involved in sensing forces in various cell types and tissues.
evidence: This is a general statement about Piezo1 function that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The Piezo1 structure is bowl-shaped.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy has revealed that the Piezo1 structure is bowl-shaped and capable of inducing membrane curvature via its extended footprint
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to cryo-electron microscopy studies.

claim: Piezo1 is capable of inducing membrane curvature via its extended footprint.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy has revealed that the Piezo1 structure is bowl-shaped and capable of inducing membrane curvature via its extended footprint
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to cryo-electron microscopy studies.

claim: At endogenous densities (1–2 channels/μm2), Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity.
source: Our data, together with stochastic simulations of Piezo1 spatial distributions, show that both at endogenous densities (1–2 channels/μm2), and at non-physiological densities (10–100 channels/μm2) predicted to cause substantial footprint overlap, Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity or open probability in the nominal absence of membrane tension.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp electrophysiology and stochastic simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: At non-physiological densities (10–100 channels/μm2), Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity.
source: Our data, together with stochastic simulations of Piezo1 spatial distributions, show that both at endogenous densities (1–2 channels/μm2), and at non-physiological densities (10–100 channels/μm2) predicted to cause substantial footprint overlap, Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity or open probability in the nominal absence of membrane tension.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from patch-clamp electrophysiology at high channel densities.

claim: At densities of 10–100 channels/μm2, substantial footprint overlap is predicted to occur.
source: Our data, together with stochastic simulations of Piezo1 spatial distributions, show that both at endogenous densities (1–2 channels/μm2), and at non-physiological densities (10–100 channels/μm2) predicted to cause substantial footprint overlap, Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity or open probability in the nominal absence of membrane tension.
evidence: This prediction is based on theoretical calculations and stochastic simulations.

claim: Piezo1 density has no effect on open probability in the nominal absence of membrane tension.
source: Our data, together with stochastic simulations of Piezo1 spatial distributions, show that both at endogenous densities (1–2 channels/μm2), and at non-physiological densities (10–100 channels/μm2) predicted to cause substantial footprint overlap, Piezo1 density has no effect on its pressure sensitivity or open probability in the nominal absence of membrane tension.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of open probability during prepulse protocols.

claim: Piezo channels, at densities likely to be physiologically relevant, inherently behave as independent mechanotransducers.
source: The results suggest that Piezo channels, at densities likely to be physiologically relevant, inherently behave as independent mechanotransducers.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data showing no functional interactions at various densities.

claim: The independent behavior of Piezo channels is essential for cells to transduce forces homogeneously across the entire cell membrane.
source: We propose that this property is essential for cells to transduce forces homogeneously across the entire cell membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the functional independence observed in the experiments.

claim: Piezo1 is a mechanically gated cation channel that directly senses membrane tension with high sensitivity.
source: For example, Piezo1 is a mechanically gated cation channel that directly senses membrane tension (T) with high sensitivity (Coste et al., 2010; Cox et al., 2016; Lewis and Grandl, 2015; Syeda et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Any mechanical disturbance of the cell membrane may lead to changes in Piezo1 channel open probability.
source: Therefore, theoretically, any mechanical disturbance of the cell membrane may lead to changes in Piezo1 channel open probability (Po).
evidence: This is a theoretical inference based on Piezo1's mechanosensitivity.

claim: The propagation of membrane tension away from its source is relatively slow (D ~ 0.024 µm2/s).
source: However, the propagation of membrane tension away from its source has been shown to be relatively slow (D ~ 0.024 µm2/s), poising Piezo channels with the ability to efficiently and rapidly transduce only mechanical forces that are nearby (Shi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Piezo channels can efficiently and rapidly transduce only mechanical forces that are nearby.
source: However, the propagation of membrane tension away from its source has been shown to be relatively slow (D ~ 0.024 µm2/s), poising Piezo channels with the ability to efficiently and rapidly transduce only mechanical forces that are nearby (Shi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the slow propagation of membrane tension.

claim: The degree to which forces are transduced homogeneously across the cell membrane depends on the spatial distribution of force-gated ion channels.
source: The degree to which forces are transduced homogeneously across the cell membrane likely depends not only on the dynamics of membrane tension propagation, but also on (i) the spatial distribution of force-gated ion channels, and (ii) on their functional independence.
evidence: This is a logical inference about factors affecting force transduction.

claim: The degree to which forces are transduced homogeneously across the cell membrane depends on the functional independence of force-gated ion channels.
source: The degree to which forces are transduced homogeneously across the cell membrane likely depends not only on the dynamics of membrane tension propagation, but also on (i) the spatial distribution of force-gated ion channels, and (ii) on their functional independence.
evidence: This is a logical inference about factors affecting force transduction.

claim: TIRF imaging revealed free diffusion of Piezo1 channels over the surface of live neural stem/progenitor cells.
source: TIRF imaging of Piezo1 channels revealed their free diffusion over the surface of live neural stem/progenitor cells, indirectly suggesting channels are not tethered to other static structures and that random membrane distribution may be possible. However, in the same cells, Piezo1-related activity was spatially enriched, which could arise from non-uniform distribution of Piezo1 channels, variable membrane tension, or both (Ellefsen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous imaging study.

claim: Piezo1 channels are not tethered to other static structures.
source: TIRF imaging of Piezo1 channels revealed their free diffusion over the surface of live neural stem/progenitor cells, indirectly suggesting channels are not tethered to other static structures and that random membrane distribution may be possible. However, in the same cells, Piezo1-related activity was spatially enriched, which could arise from non-uniform distribution of Piezo1 channels, variable membrane tension, or both (Ellefsen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of free diffusion.

claim: Piezo1-related activity was spatially enriched in neural stem/progenitor cells.
source: TIRF imaging of Piezo1 channels revealed their free diffusion over the surface of live neural stem/progenitor cells, indirectly suggesting channels are not tethered to other static structures and that random membrane distribution may be possible. However, in the same cells, Piezo1-related activity was spatially enriched, which could arise from non-uniform distribution of Piezo1 channels, variable membrane tension, or both (Ellefsen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: STORM imaging of HEK293 cells stably expressing GFP-tagged Piezo1 suggested a non-homogenous spatial distribution.
source: STORM imaging of HEK293 cells stably expressing GFP-tagged Piezo1 also suggested a non-homogenous spatial distribution, but at channel densities that are likely not physiological (Ridone et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous imaging study.

claim: The non-homogenous distribution observed in STORM imaging was at channel densities that are likely not physiological.
source: STORM imaging of HEK293 cells stably expressing GFP-tagged Piezo1 also suggested a non-homogenous spatial distribution, but at channel densities that are likely not physiological (Ridone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cited study's findings.

claim: Piezo1 may be concentrated at focal adhesions.
source: Additional studies have proposed the existence of clusters with varying numbers of channels (Jiang et al., 2021), and that Piezo1 may be concentrated at focal adhesions (Mingxi Yao et al., 2020) and at wound edges in keratinocytes (Holt et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Piezo1 may be concentrated at wound edges in keratinocytes.
source: Additional studies have proposed the existence of clusters with varying numbers of channels (Jiang et al., 2021), and that Piezo1 may be concentrated at focal adhesions (Mingxi Yao et al., 2020) and at wound edges in keratinocytes (Holt et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy structures revealed Piezo1's large and extremely curved dome-shaped structure.
source: A compelling theoretical framework predicting spatial and functional interactions between nearby Piezo channels has been constructed based on cryo-electron microscopy structures of Piezo1, which revealed its large and extremely curved dome-shaped structure (Guo and MacKinnon, 2017; Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018; Saotome et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to cryo-EM studies.

claim: Piezo1 can both sense and curve the proximal membrane with a characteristic decay length extending ~14 nm beyond the channel.
source: Theoretical calculations based on these structures suggest that Piezo1 can both sense and curve the proximal membrane with a characteristic decay length extending ~14 nm beyond the channel.
evidence: This claim is based on theoretical calculations from cited studies.

claim: Piezo1 channels that are within ~3 decay lengths (a 'footprint' of ~50 nm) may influence each other via multiple mechanisms.
source: The energetic cost of this membrane curvature implies that Piezo1 channels that are within ~3 decay lengths (a 'footprint' of ~50 nm; see Materials and methods) may influence each other via multiple mechanisms: opposing curvature may cause nearby Piezo1 channels to repel each other, as well as influence each other's gating properties (Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on membrane energetics calculations.

claim: Opposing curvature may cause nearby Piezo1 channels to repel each other.
source: The energetic cost of this membrane curvature implies that Piezo1 channels that are within ~3 decay lengths (a 'footprint' of ~50 nm; see Materials and methods) may influence each other via multiple mechanisms: opposing curvature may cause nearby Piezo1 channels to repel each other, as well as influence each other's gating properties (Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from cited work.

claim: Nearby Piezo1 channels may influence each other's gating properties.
source: The energetic cost of this membrane curvature implies that Piezo1 channels that are within ~3 decay lengths (a 'footprint' of ~50 nm; see Materials and methods) may influence each other via multiple mechanisms: opposing curvature may cause nearby Piezo1 channels to repel each other, as well as influence each other's gating properties (Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from cited work.

claim: Imaging of vesicles containing reconstituted Piezo1 demonstrated the ability of Piezo1 to curve the membrane locally.
source: Indeed, imaging of vesicles containing reconstituted Piezo1 has demonstrated the ability of Piezo1 to curve the membrane locally and suggested that flattening of the channel dome may directly couple to channel opening, but the precise effects of membrane energetics on gating have yet to be explored experimentally (Jiang et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to reconstitution studies.

claim: Flattening of the channel dome may directly couple to channel opening.
source: Indeed, imaging of vesicles containing reconstituted Piezo1 has demonstrated the ability of Piezo1 to curve the membrane locally and suggested that flattening of the channel dome may directly couple to channel opening, but the precise effects of membrane energetics on gating have yet to be explored experimentally (Jiang et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a suggestion from cited reconstitution studies.

claim: The precise effects of membrane energetics on gating have yet to be explored experimentally.
source: Indeed, imaging of vesicles containing reconstituted Piezo1 has demonstrated the ability of Piezo1 to curve the membrane locally and suggested that flattening of the channel dome may directly couple to channel opening, but the precise effects of membrane energetics on gating have yet to be explored experimentally (Jiang et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Neuro2A cells natively express Piezo1.
source: To simultaneously measure and thus directly correlate Piezo1 channel density with its gating properties, we performed cell-attached patch-clamp electrophysiology on Neuro2A cells, which natively express Piezo1 (Coste et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Neuro2A cells have among the highest endogenous levels of Piezo1 expression.
source: We chose Neuro2A cells over human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and other cell lines because they have among the highest endogenous levels of Piezo1 expression, thus offering the highest likelihood for observing any potential functional effects of local channel density on function.
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on knowledge of Piezo1 expression levels.

claim: Piezo1 inactivation at +60 mV is minimal during short pressure steps.
source: Since Piezo1 inactivation precludes a precise measurement of maximal current (Imax) at negative potentials, we recorded currents at +60 mV, where inactivation during short pressure steps is minimal (Coste et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Traditional step protocols induce irreversible changes in patch geometry owing to membrane creep, particularly at positive voltages.
source: However, traditional step protocols are well known to induce irreversible changes in patch geometry owing to membrane creep, particularly at positive voltages (Lewis and Grandl, 2015; Suchyna et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A direct step to a saturating pressure (–60 mmHg) caused small changes in current due to leak and/or capacitance even in patches with zero channels.
source: Indeed, a direct step to a saturating pressure (–60 mmHg) caused small, but measurable changes in current due to leak and/or capacitance even in patches that were later classified to have zero channels (see below; mean ± SD: 2.6 ± 1.3 pA; n=33 patches; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The same pressure step caused a similarly small current in patches from Neuro2A-Piezo1ko cells (mean ± SD: 3.8 ± 1.5 pA, n=15 patches).
source: Consistent with this idea, the same pressure step caused a similarly small current in patches from Neuro2A-Piezo1ko cells, which have been CRISPR-engineered to lack Piezo1 channels (mean ± SD: 3.8 ± 1.5 pA, n=15 patches; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from knockout cells.

claim: A step protocol consistently overestimates current by 2–3 pA.
source: Consequently, a step protocol consistently overestimates current by 2–3 pA, and thus channel numbers accordingly (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental observations of background current.

claim: Pressure equilibration occurs within ~7 ms.
source: The total duration of this ramp is short enough to minimize membrane creep (3 s), but each step is long enough (50 ms) to allow pressure equilibration, which occurs within ~7 ms (Lewis et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Inactivation of Piezo1 at +60 mV is minimal (step pulse: mean current at 200 ms = 96.5±7.4% of peak; n=281 patches).
source: Importantly, the step pulse allowed us to confirm post hoc that inactivation of Piezo1 at this voltage is minimal (step pulse: mean current at 200 ms = 96.5±7.4% of peak; n=281 patches; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements.

claim: The mean single-channel current from all patches with one channel is i=0.98±0.04 pA (n=35 patches).
source: We next used the mean single-channel current from all patches with one channel (i=0.98±0.04 pA, n=35 patches; Figure 1—figure supplement 2G) to calculate the precise number of channels (n=Imax/i) in all other patches.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from experimental data.

claim: The distribution average of Piezo1 channel numbers per patch was 3.5±3.1 channels.
source: Ultimately, we obtained a continuous, bell-shaped distribution of Piezo1 channel numbers per patch (Figure 1E). The distribution average was 3.5±3.1 channels per patch, which given our small pipette sizes is consistent with previously reported levels of expression in Neuro2A cells (Coste et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statistical summary of experimental measurements.

claim: The dome size of membrane patches inside patch pipettes is estimated to be 2 µm.
source: We estimated the dome size of membrane patches inside patch pipettes from imaging experiments to be 2 µm (see Materials and methods) and used this value to calculate the average density of Piezo1 channels to be 1–2 channels/µm2.
evidence: This is an estimate based on imaging experiments.

claim: The average density of Piezo1 channels in Neuro2A cells is 1–2 channels/µm2.
source: We estimated the dome size of membrane patches inside patch pipettes from imaging experiments to be 2 µm (see Materials and methods) and used this value to calculate the average density of Piezo1 channels to be 1–2 channels/µm2.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements of channel number and patch size.

claim: For patches containing 1–14 channels, average P50 values do not vary substantially with channel number.
source: Altogether, the results show that, for patches containing 1–14 channels, average P50 values do not vary substantially with channel number (Figure 1F).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: P50 and slope (k) values are virtually identical for patches containing 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 channels.
source: Visual inspection as well as fits with sigmoidal functions show that P50 and slope (k) values are virtually identical for patches containing 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 channels (1 channel: P50=–23.2 mmHg, k=–3.3 mmHg; 5 channels: P50=–23.7 mmHg, k=–4.2 mmHg).
evidence: This is based on analysis of idealized traces and sigmoidal fits to the data.

claim: At densities of up to 2 channels/µm2, Piezo1 channels do not influence each other's mechanosensitivity.
source: We therefore conclude from both analyses that at densities of up to 2 channels/µm2, Piezo1 channels do not influence each other's mechanosensitivity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from multiple analyses of experimental data.

claim: In Neuro2A cells, Piezo1 channels may be homogeneously distributed across the cell surface.
source: The resulting distribution fits the experimental data reasonably well, indicating that in Neuro2A cells, Piezo1 channels may be homogenously distributed across the cell surface, rather than being spatially localized in close proximity (Figure 3A–F).
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparison of experimental data with stochastic simulations.

claim: A distribution in which on average 1.6 Piezo1 channels interact over 50 nm also describes the experimental data well.
source: Strikingly, a distribution in which on average 1.6 Piezo1 channels (drawn from a Poisson distribution centered at 1; see Materials and methods) interact over 50 nm also describes the experimental data well.
evidence: This is based on stochastic modeling that fits the experimental data.

claim: Simulating larger channel clusters (n ~ 5) fails to reproduce the experimental distribution.
source: However, simulating larger channel clusters (n ~ 5) fails to reproduce the experimental distribution, specifically the probability of capturing patches without any channels (Figure 3A–F).
evidence: This is based on comparison of simulation results with experimental data.

claim: In a truly random distribution, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is ~390 nm.
source: Interestingly, the two distributions differ significantly in the predicted fraction of channels that are within one footprint of at least one other channel: in a truly random distribution, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is ~390 nm, and only ~5% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel
evidence: This is a prediction from stochastic modeling.

claim: In a truly random distribution, only ~5% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel.
source: Interestingly, the two distributions differ significantly in the predicted fraction of channels that are within one footprint of at least one other channel: in a truly random distribution, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is ~390 nm, and only ~5% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel
evidence: This is a prediction from stochastic modeling.

claim: If channels tend to cluster in groups of 2–3, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is reduced to 225 nm.
source: whereas if channels tend to cluster in groups of 2–3, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is reduced to 225 nm and almost 50% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is a prediction from stochastic modeling with clustering.

claim: If channels tend to cluster in groups of 2–3, almost 50% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel.
source: whereas if channels tend to cluster in groups of 2–3, the mean nearest-neighbor distance is reduced to 225 nm and almost 50% of channels are within 100 nm of another channel (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is a prediction from stochastic modeling with clustering.

claim: If spatial localization of Piezo1 in groups of 2-3 occurs, it does not have a substantial effect on Piezo1 pressure sensitivity.
source: However, our functional data support the idea that if the latter spatial localization indeed occurs, it does not have a substantial effect on Piezo1 pressure sensitivity (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the functional data showing no effect of channel number on pressure sensitivity.

claim: Transfection with Lipofectamine 2000 maximizes channel density 42–48 hr post-transfection.
source: In pilot experiments, we found that transfection with Lipofectamine 2000 maximizes channel density 42–48 hr post-transfection (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on pilot experimental observations.

claim: Overexpression yields peak currents that inactivate to a larger extent even at +60 mV.
source: We first repeated our previous ramp protocol, but found that while overexpression yields peak currents that are much larger, these currents inactivate to a larger extent even at +60 mV, such that a ramp protocol substantially underestimates the total number of channels in the patch (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; current at 200 ms=53.3±18.1% of peak, n=138 patches).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from overexpression experiments.

claim: The number of channels per patch in overexpression experiments was well described by a Gaussian distribution with 89.2±49.8 channels per patch.
source: The number of channels per patch was well described by a Gaussian distribution with 89.2±49.8 channels per patch (Figure 4C), which we estimate corresponds to a Piezo1 density of ~45 channels/µm2 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a statistical summary of experimental measurements.

claim: The average Piezo1 density in overexpression experiments is ~45 channels/µm2.
source: The number of channels per patch was well described by a Gaussian distribution with 89.2±49.8 channels per patch (Figure 4C), which we estimate corresponds to a Piezo1 density of ~45 channels/µm2 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements.

claim: The most extreme current amplitude observed (–190 pA, or ~200 channels) corresponds to a maximal density of ~100 channels/µm2.
source: The most extreme current amplitude we observed (–190 pA, or ~200 channels) corresponds to a maximal density of ~100 channels/µm2.
evidence: This is calculated from the maximum observed current.

claim: At a density of ~100 channels/µm2, if Piezo channels were randomly distributed, their mean next-neighbor distance would be ~50 nm.
source: At this maximal density, if Piezo channels were randomly distributed in the membrane, their mean next-neighbor distance would be ~50 nm (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed density.

claim: At high densities, Piezos are likely in close enough proximity to influence each other's function.
source: This calculation suggests that we have reached densities in which Piezos are likely in close enough proximity to influence each other's function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the calculated nearest-neighbor distances.

claim: Piezo1 open probability was generally small (<1%) during the prepulse.
source: We found that open probability was generally small (<1%), which was consistent with previous work in our lab (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with previous work.

claim: Piezo1 open probability slightly decreased with channel density, from 0.6±0.4% for patches with 1–10 channels to 0.2±0.1% for patches with >200 channels.
source: Most notably however, we found that Piezo1 open probability did not increase with channel density; rather, open probability slightly decreased, from 0.6±0.4% for patches with 1–10 channels (mean ± SD; n=3 patches) to 0.2±0.1% for patches with >200 channels (n=3 patches) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the data.

claim: Both slope and P50 values were unaffected by channel number in overexpression experiments.
source: Both slope and P50 values were unaffected by channel number (Figure 4E–F), and these values were also unaffected by pipette size (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C-D).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from analysis of experimental data.

claim: Pressure-response curves and sensitivity (slope) are independent of channel numbers.
source: The results again show that pressure-response curves and sensitivity (slope) are independent of channel numbers (for 0–20 channels, P50=–21.5 mmHg, k=–8.0 mmHg, n=5; for >200 channels, P50=–21.0 mmHg, k=–6.8 mmHg, n=3).
evidence: This conclusion is based on analysis of normalized pressure-response curves.

claim: There is no correlation between either T50 or the slope (k) and channel density in the range of 10–70 channels/µm2.
source: Importantly, we found no correlation between either the tension of half-maximal activation (T50) or the slope (k) and channel density in the range of 10–70 channels/µm2 (Figure 5D–F), again supporting that Piezo1 channels do not influence each other's tension sensitivity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from imaging experiments combined with electrophysiology.

claim: In wild-type Neuro2A cells, most Piezo1 channels are too far apart to 'feel' each other.
source: In other words, in wild-type Neuro2A cells, most Piezo1 channels are too far apart to 'feel' each other.
evidence: This is an inference from the spatial distribution modeling and experimental data.

claim: Piezo1 channels have no strong intrinsic tendency to spatially concentrate.
source: This result is important, because it shows that Piezo1 channels have no strong intrinsic tendency to spatially concentrate and functionally modulate each other's mechanical sensitivity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental observations and modeling.

claim: Piezo1 channels have no strong intrinsic tendency to functionally modulate each other's mechanical sensitivity.
source: This result is important, because it shows that Piezo1 channels have no strong intrinsic tendency to spatially concentrate and functionally modulate each other's mechanical sensitivity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental observations showing no functional interactions.

claim: The independent behavior of Piezo1 channels is ideal for a cell to transduce mechanical forces homogeneously.
source: Both of these properties are ideal for a cell in order to transduce mechanical forces homogeneously.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the findings.

claim: In the nominal absence of membrane tension, Piezo1 open probability is slightly (~0.5%) reduced with channel number but overall very low (<1%) at all channel densities probed.
source: Surprisingly, our data do suggest that in the nominal absence of membrane tension Piezo1 open probability is slightly (~0.5%) reduced with channel number but overall, very low (<1%) at all channel densities we probed.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Simulations of Piezo1 in extreme proximity (1–3 nm dome-dome distance) showed the opposite result regarding open probability.
source: This is notable, because the opposite result was recently obtained by simulations of Piezo1 that are in extreme proximity to each other (1–3 nm dome-dome distance; Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison with results from a cited simulation study.

claim: Calcium permeating through Piezo1 may influence the resting open probability of nearby channels.
source: Moreover, any cooperativity need not arise via membrane footprint interactions: for example, calcium permeating through Piezo1 may influence the resting open probability of nearby channels.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation for potential cooperativity.

claim: Calcium-induced cooperativity is a well-known phenomenon in other ion channels, such as TRPA1.
source: Indeed, calcium-induced cooperativity is a well-known phenomenon in other ion channels, such as TRPA1 (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a study on TRPA1.

claim: The conclusions may be applicable to other cell types that express Piezos at levels similar or lower to that of Neuro2A cells.
source: Altogether, our conclusions may be applicable to other cell types that express Piezos at levels similar or lower to that of Neuro2A cells.
evidence: This is a speculative extrapolation of the findings to other cell types.

claim: Specific cell types may concentrate Piezo channels into locations dedicated to detecting forces.
source: However, we fully expect that specific cell types may concentrate Piezo channels into locations that are dedicated to detecting forces.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential cell-type-specific mechanisms.

claim: If Piezo clustering is observed, it would require a dedicated mechanism that is not Piezo-intrinsic, such as a tethering molecule.
source: However, our work directly predicts that if such a clustering was indeed observed, it would require a dedicated mechanism that is not Piezo-intrinsic, such as a still elusive tethering molecule.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the findings that Piezo1 has no intrinsic clustering tendency.

claim: The characteristic decay length (λ) of membrane deformation induced by Piezo1 is estimated to be 14 nm.
source: The characteristic decay length (λ) of membrane deformation induced by the large curved dome of Piezo1 is estimated to be 14 nm (Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018).
evidence: This is based on theoretical calculations from a cited study.

claim: The approximate total membrane footprint of Piezo1 is ~50 nm.
source: We put upper bounds of possible Piezo energetic interactions due to membrane curvature beyond the dome itself as 3× this decay length; when adding this to the radius of the channel dome, this yields an approximate total membrane footprint of (10 nm +3*14 nm ~ 50 nm).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the decay length and channel dome size.

claim: Patch domes from pipettes 3 to 6 MΩ have an approximate surface area of 2 µm2.
source: From our imaging data (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), we estimated that patch domes from pipettes 3 to 6 MΩ have an approximate surface area of 2 µm2.
evidence: This is an estimate from imaging experiments.

claim: If the patch dome is approximated as a flat circle with surface area 2 µm2, this corresponds to a pipette radius of 0.8 µm.
source: If the patch dome is approximated as a flat circle, this corresponds to a pipette radius of 0.8 µm, which was used for simulation of Piezo1 spatial distribution in the Thomas point process model.
evidence: This is a geometric calculation from the surface area estimate.

claim: At maximal overexpression density, approximately 4% of the membrane surface would be covered by Piezo channels.
source: For the maximal channel number we observed (~200 channels), with an estimated in-plane area of 400 nm2 (Wang et al., 2019), an estimated footprint of 7800 nm2 (calculated from a footprint of 50 nm; Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018) and a patch dome surface area of 2 µm2, approximately 4% of the membrane surface would be covered by Piezo channels and 78% of the surface covered by Piezos + corresponding footprints if channels were evenly distributed (with no overlap of footprints).
evidence: This is a calculation based on channel dimensions and density.

claim: At maximal overexpression density, 78% of the membrane surface would be covered by Piezos plus corresponding footprints if channels were evenly distributed.
source: For the maximal channel number we observed (~200 channels), with an estimated in-plane area of 400 nm2 (Wang et al., 2019), an estimated footprint of 7800 nm2 (calculated from a footprint of 50 nm; Haselwandter and MacKinnon, 2018) and a patch dome surface area of 2 µm2, approximately 4% of the membrane surface would be covered by Piezo channels and 78% of the surface covered by Piezos + corresponding footprints if channels were evenly distributed (with no overlap of footprints).
evidence: This is a calculation based on channel dimensions, footprint size, and density.

claim: ~15% of patches in wild-type Neuro2A cells contained no Piezo1 channels.
